title: ICU Workflow — Admission, Rounding, Signout
sources: Critical Vector — ICU Workflow: Admission · Pre-Rounding · Signout
I-PASS Study Group (handoff bundle — 23% error reduction); ABCDEF bundle cohort (n=15,226)

changelog.change: Initial entry — converted from the CV ICU workflow guide: FAST HUGS BID admission checklist, the 5-step pre-round, and the I-PASS signout framework.

summary: Every ICU shift is three structural moments — build the plan (admission), prepare to defend it (pre-round), hand it off (signout). The quality of the signout is downstream of the quality of the admission orders. FAST HUGS BID on admission; I-PASS at handoff.

rows: Enteral nutrition within 24–48 h; trophic feeds acceptable initially. Hold for active UGI bleed or escalating pressors.
Pain first — CPOT (intubated) or NRS (awake). Treat pain before sedating.
Light target: RASS 0 to −1. Daily spontaneous awakening trial (SAT). Deep sedation independently worsens outcomes.
Pharmacologic backbone: enoxaparin 40 mg SC daily or UFH 5,000 U SC q8–12 h. Reassess bleeding risk daily — it is dynamic. IPC benefit is population-dependent (below).
≥ 30° in every ventilated patient — free VAP prevention.
Pantoprazole for ventilated / coagulopathic / shock / AKI-on-RRT patients. REVISE (n=4,821): clinically important GI bleed 1.0% vs 3.5% (HR 0.30); no difference in 90-day mortality, VAP, or C. diff.
Target 140–180 mg/dL. NICE-SUGAR: tight control (81–108) increased mortality — abandoned as standard practice.
Daily spontaneous breathing trial, paired with the SAT, in every ventilated patient.
Senna + PRN bisacodyl / PEG at admission — opioids + immobility = obstipation.
Daily necessity review for every line, tube, and catheter — remove what isn't needed.
Review cultures at 48–72 h; narrow or stop antibiotics if the trajectory permits.

body.text: VTE prophylaxis nuance: in surgical / trauma cohorts, combined IPC + pharmacologic prophylaxis reduces symptomatic PE (OR 0.39) vs pharmacologic alone — but in the medical ICU, adding IPC to heparin showed NO reduction in proximal DVT (3.9% vs 4.2%). Use IPC as the sole method only when pharmacologic prophylaxis is contraindicated.
Pre-rounding is not re-rounding. The objective is a current clinical snapshot and a defensible plan. Start with your sickest patient, not room one — cognitive bandwidth is highest early in the shift.

items: 1. Triage (~2 min) — acuity before touching a chart.

2. Chart review (~5 min) — overnight events (nursing notes, pages, new orders); vitals TREND not just the last reading; vent settings (mode, rate, FiO2, PEEP, Vt, plateau); 24-h fluid balance + UOP/hr + total since admission; pending cultures, morning labs, drip rates.

3. Bedside assessment (non-negotiable) — the patient (colour, work of breathing, cap refill, gross neuro); the monitor (rhythm, SpO2 and arterial-line waveforms); the pumps (running rate matches the order); drains/lines (chest-tube output, Foley, NG position).

4. Organ-system synthesis — Neuro: RASS, CAM-ICU, pain score. Pulm: vent settings, ABG/SpO2 trend, SBT candidate? CV: MAP, pressor trend, rhythm, fluid balance. Renal/Heme/ID/Endo: Cr/UOP, Hgb/plt, antibiotic day count, glucose.

5. Liberation-bundle check (ABCDEF — associated with lower 7-day mortality, n=15,226): A pain assessed? B both SAT + SBT done? C sedation minimised? D CAM-ICU done? E mobility plan? F family updated, goals documented?

body.text: Miscommunication contributes to ~1/3 of serious medical errors. I-PASS: 23% reduction in medical errors, 30% reduction in preventable adverse events, no increase in handoff time.

rows: One-word label: Fair (stable) / Watcher (could change — check hourly) / Unstable (actively requiring intervention) / Discharge-Comfort.
One-liner + systems-based key details: hemodynamics, vent, ID, renal, code status.
Specific, time-bound tasks — 'repeat lactate at 22:00', 'if UOP < 30 mL/hr ×2 h, give 500 mL LR'. NOT 'keep an eye on things'.
IF/THEN contingency statements — 'IF MAP < 65 despite norepinephrine at 15, THEN start vasopressin and repeat lactate'. A playbook, not a prediction.
The read-back — the receiver restates the key issues to close the loop before anyone leaves.

buildNote: Tier 3. FAST HUGS BID is a checklist-shaped candidate for a Procedures `workflow`-type module if the app wants it interactive rather than as a reference table.
